title: Kernel Selector v2 — Metrics Cardinality Review (instrumentation notes)
body:
Meeting: selector v2 metrics/trace instrumentation review (cardinality + standards)
Date: 2026-01-23
Attendees: Thomas Baird (Metrics cardinality controls), Logan Wright (Telemetry platform), Allison Grant (Observability standards), Grace Kim (Kernel selection lead), Omar El-Sayed (Runtime integration), Nadia Rahman (Cost/latency attribution), Aisha Bello (SRE dashboards/alerts), Sana Farid (Canary analysis)

Context / why we’re here
- Selector v2 adds rich decision telemetry: selector version, model family, GPU SKU normalization, seq-length bucket, selected kernel id, and fallback path.
- Early implementation draft (ENG-3927 / PR 18493) risked high label cardinality from:
  - raw model_name / model_version labels
  - raw kernel_id and per-build kernel variant strings
  - per-host GPU identifiers (device UUIDs, MIG slices)
  - raw prompt length / context length numeric values
  - region/cluster/customer labels on “always-on” metrics
- Goal: preserve debuggability while making metrics safe to ship broadly (Hosted + Dedicated) without blowing Prometheus/Mimir/OTel backend limits or making dashboards unusable.

Scope reviewed
- Metrics: counters + histograms + exemplars around selection events
- Logs/events: structured selection decision event (sampled)
- Traces: span attributes on request spans and optional child span for selection logic

Decision summary (what we agreed to ship)
1) Metrics MUST be low-cardinality and only use allowed label set (below). Anything else goes to sampled event logs or traces.
2) Use bucketing/enums for potentially large domains: GPU, seq length, route tier.
3) Kernel identifier handling:
   - Metrics: use a stable, small enum (kernel_family) by default.
   - Traces/log events: may include full kernel_id for “why did this happen” debugging.
4) Model identifier handling:
   - Metrics: model_family only (NOT model_name).
   - Traces/log events: can include model_id/model_name behind sampling and redaction rules.
5) Sampling strategy is required for selection decision events; default-on only for canary/debug.

Allowed label set (metrics)
These are the ONLY labels permitted on kernel-selection metrics that are emitted on every request (no sampling):
- selector_version: {"v1", "v2"}
- selection_result: {"selected", "fallback_v1", "fallback_safe_set", "error"}
- model_family: enum from taxonomy (e.g., "llama", "mistral", "qwen", "unknown")
- seq_bucket: enum (see below)
- gpu_sku: normalized enum (see below)
- runtime_regime: {"prefill", "decode"} (only if reliably populated; else "unknown")
- quantization: {"fp16", "bf16", "int8", "int4", "unknown"} (only if already low-cardinality and stable)

Explicitly NOT allowed as metric labels
- model_name, model_id, model_revision, model_sha
- raw kernel_id (full string), kernel_build_id, kernel_commit
- request_id, user_id, org_id/customer_id, project_id
- host_id, pod_name, node_name, gpu_uuid, device_index
- region/cluster/az labels on high-volume per-request metrics (allowed only in infrastructure-level dashboards, not on selection metrics)
- any numeric labels (prompt_tokens, context_length, batch_size) — must be bucketed

Seq-length + batching bucketing
We need to answer “does v2 help for short vs long prompts” without emitting raw lengths.
Agreed on the following bucket dimensions:
- runtime_regime:
  - prefill = first token / prompt processing
  - decode = subsequent tokens
- seq_bucket (effective context length at time of kernel choice):
  - s0_0_256
  - s1_257_1024
  - s2_1025_4096
  - s3_4097_8192
  - s4_8193_16384
  - s5_16385_plus
Notes:
- Names are intentionally stable strings (not derived from runtime config) to prevent “bucket drift” across deploys.
- Off-by-one boundary rule documented for scheduler/runtime integration: boundary is inclusive on lower bound, inclusive on upper bound (e.g., 0–256, 257–1024). If implementation needs inclusive/exclusive for speed, it MUST map back to the stable names.
- Separate metric/histogram for “bucket_unknown” to catch missing signals without contaminating other buckets.

GPU SKU normalization bucketing
We need stable buckets across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private, including MIG/partitioned environments.
gpu_sku label must be normalized to one of:
- l4
- a10
- a100_40g
- a100_80g
- h100_sxm
- h100_pcie
- other_sm80
- other_sm90
- unknown
Notes:
- If MIG is detected, do NOT append MIG profile as a label. Instead set gpu_sku as above and add a sampled debug field (see below) for MIG profile.
- “other_smXX” is used to preserve some capability grouping without exploding SKU list.
- Any new GPU type requires adding to normalization map + a brief note in runtime release notes.

Kernel identifier representation
- Metrics will use kernel_family (coarse grouping) instead of kernel_id:
  - kernel_family examples: "flashattn_v2", "flashattn_v3", "xformers", "triton_sdpa", "cutlass_prefill", "safe_baseline"
- Traces and selection decision events may include:
  - kernel_id (full string)
  - kernel_registry_version
  - kernel_entry_key (table row key)
but ONLY under sampling rules.

Metric set (proposed)
Naming not final; purpose reviewed and approved.
- counter: runtime_kernel_selection_total{selector_version,selection_result,model_family,seq_bucket,gpu_sku,runtime_regime,quantization}
- histogram: runtime_kernel_selection_latency_ms_bucket{selector_version,model_family,seq_bucket,gpu_sku,runtime_regime}
  - This is latency of selection logic only (not model inference). Keep buckets coarse; we only need to catch pathological slow paths.
- counter: runtime_kernel_selection_unknowns_total{unknown_type=("model_family"|"gpu_sku"|"seq_bucket"|"regime")}
- counter: runtime_kernel_selection_fallback_total{fallback_type=("v1"|"safe_set"|"registry_miss"|"capability_mismatch")}

Trace + event fields (sampled)
These fields are useful for debugging and can be high-cardinality. Agreed these are OK ONLY in traces and/or a sampled structured event.
- model_name / model_id
- full kernel_id
- selection_path (string like: "registry_hit->capability_ok->picked_fastest")
- registry_row_key
- gpu_name_raw (from driver)
- mig_profile (if present)
- prompt_tokens / context_length raw numbers
- batch_size, microbatch_size, continuous_batching_state
- override_applied (boolean) + override_source ("config"|"emergency"|"experiment")

Sampling / emission rules
- selection decision event (structured log/event):
  - default sampling: 0.1% (1e-3) on Hosted; 0% on Dedicated unless enabled by operator
  - on error/fallback_safe_set: sample at 100% (these are rare and important)
  - on canary cohort (selector v2 enabled): increase to 1% temporarily during rollout windows
- traces:
  - add low-cardinality span attributes always (selector_version, selection_result, model_family, seq_bucket, gpu_sku)
  - attach high-cardinality attributes only when trace is already sampled OR when selection_result != selected

Dashboards / queries (what SRE wants to see)
Aisha requested the following views (INT-2331):
- selector version breakdown over time (v1 vs v2) + fallback rates
- kernel_family heatmap by {model_family, seq_bucket, gpu_sku}
- p95 end-to-end inference latency segmented by selector_version (using existing inference metrics; avoid adding selector labels to those histograms)
- alert: spike in fallback_safe_set rate OR spike in unknown bucket rate

Open questions / follow-ups
- Do we need quantization label on selection metrics?
  - Nadia’s view: useful for cost/latency attribution, but only if it’s a small stable set.
  - Action: keep behind config flag; default off until verified low-cardinality in prod.
- Are we confident runtime_regime is always set correctly?
  - Omar to validate scheduler integration; until then, allow "unknown" and track unknown rate.

Action items
- Thomas Baird: write up allowed label policy + rationale in the telemetry standards doc and link from ENG-3927 (Due 2026-01-27)
- Logan Wright: confirm backend label limits + add automated lint check for disallowed labels in OTel/Prom metrics pipeline (Due 2026-02-05)
- Grace Kim + Omar El-Sayed: implement kernel_family mapping and ensure kernel_id never appears in metrics labels (Due 2026-02-02)
- Omar El-Sayed + Lena Fischer: ensure seq_bucket naming matches agreed stable strings; add unit tests for boundaries (Due 2026-02-06)
- Aisha Bello: update runtime performance dashboard template with selector panels (INT-2331) (Due 2026-02-10)
- Sana Farid: define canary checklist items for “cardinality smoke check” (series count, top label values) as part of rollout (Due 2026-02-07)

Notes / reminders
- If we need deeper per-model debugging, do it via (a) sampled events, (b) ad-hoc debug endpoint (ENG-3932), or (c) temporary canary-only metrics with explicit TTL and removal plan.
- Any time we add a new label to the selection metrics, it must go through this same review (Thomas + Logan + Allison) before merging.

Appendix: quick “do / don’t”
- DO: model_family, gpu_sku (normalized), seq_bucket, selector_version
- DON’T: model_name, kernel_id, region/cluster/customer, gpu_uuid, raw prompt length
